voyage.name: Open Air Museum of Ethnography
voyage.address: Kus Tba 1 (1 Turtle Lake Road, Tortoise pond lane) კუსტბის გზა #1)
voyage.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum. "Skansen"-type museum with 70 houses and other buildings characteristic of the various parts of Georgia, plus household gadgetry and craft tools. The houses are in variable states of repair, some are tumbledown but especially those near the entry gate are okay and with helpful docents. Allow a half day for a visit, a quiet escape from the city.

voyage.name: Museum of Fine Arts
voyage.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum. Large permanent collection from antiquity to present.

voyage.name: Tbilisi History Museum
voyage.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum.

voyage.name: Museum of Georgia
voyage.alt: საქართველოს ისტორიის ჯანაშიას სახ. მუზეუმი, Simon Janashia Museum
voyage.price: Adults 7 lari, students 1 lari, guided tour in English 45 lari
voyage.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum, the Museum of Georgia houses Caucasian artefacts of archaeology and ethnography. A permanent exposition follows developments from the Bronze Age to the early 20th century. Gold was mined and worked here from a very early date - it was probably the origin of the "Golden Fleece" legend - so the area developed its own style, which influenced Achaemenid and Hellenistic jewellery. The

voyage.name: Puppet Museum
voyage.content: Several visitors in summer 2018 found it closed.

voyage.name: Galaktion Tabidze Museum
voyage.content: The museum of the eminent Georgian poet, Galaktion Tabidze (1892-1959).

voyage.name: Tbilisi Art Gallery
voyage.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum. Extensive permanent collection, plus rotating exhibitions usually featuring Georgian artists.

voyage.name: State Academy of Arts
voyage.content: It's a working university, not a public gallery, but you may be able to peek in at the historic buildings.

voyage.name: Jewish History Museum
voyage.alt: ებრაელთა ისტორიის მუზეუმი David Baazov Museum
voyage.content: Depicts the Jews in Georgia from earliest historic times to the present day. Rabbi David Baazov (1883-1947) was sent to Siberia during Stalin's purges, and his son was shot, but he survived to return to Tbilisi. The museum collection became a diaspora (notably to Rochester, Minnesota) but has been repatriated.

voyage.name: U. Japaridze House-Museum
voyage.content: Part of Georgian National Museum. Home of distinguished painter Ucha Japaridze (1906-1988).

voyage.name: E. Akhvlediani House-Museum
voyage.content: Part of the Georgian National Museum. Showcases the work of painter Elene Akhvlediani (1898-1975).

voyage.name: Open air carriage exhibition
voyage.content: In a strip of garden in the middle of a busy road, there are several carriages and wine making tools in exhibit.

voyage.name: Writer's House of Georgia
voyage.hours: 11 AM to 6 PM -- you may have to ring the door bell
voyage.content: Beautiful mansion and a focal point of Georgian literature. The house was built by David Sarajishvili, an entrepreneur, between 1903-1905, by a German architect, Karl Zaar, and combines art nouveau with neobaroque style elements. The terrace mosaic is made from tiles by Villeroy and Boch. The Writer's House was a location in which major figures of Georgian literature, such as the Blue Horns group, met in the early 19

voyage.name: Mamadaviti
voyage.content: Constructed in 1859–1871, domed in 1879.

voyage.name: Sameba Cathedral
voyage.alt: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi, Georgian: თბილისის წმინდა სამების საკათედრო ტაძარი Thbilisis cminda samebis sakathedro tadzari
voyage.content: Constructed between 1995 and 2004, it is the third-tallest Eastern Orthodox cathedral in the world. Sameba is a synthesis of traditional styles dominating the Georgian church architecture at various stages in history and has some Byzantine undertones. voyage.name: Metekhi Church ("Church of Assumption")
voyage.content: Goes back to the reign of St. Demeritus II. late 13th century. Rebuilt 17th century. Unusual in design.

voyage.name: Ascension Catholic Church of the Virgin Mary?
voyage.alt: Tbilisi Virgin Mary Church, მარიამ ღვთისმშობლის ამაღლების კათოლიკური ეკლესია
voyage.content: The church was built, which starts from the 13th century. The church is an example of eclectic architecture and has been built with pseudo-gothic and Baroco elements. The interior is decorated with thematic vitrages. Height: 23 m.

voyage.name: Anchiskhati ("Basilica of St. Mary")
voyage.content: Constructed began at the time of king Dachi Ujarmeli in the 6th century. This is the oldest church in town. Anchiskhati Basilica is a three-span basilica, divided by two abutments forming horseshoe shaped conches, which indicates the antiquity of its construction. Originally constructed of blocks of yellow tuff stone, the 1958–1964 restoration made extensive use of brick. The structure has entrances on three sides, b

voyage.name: Kashveti Church of St. George
voyage.alt: Qashveti, Georgian: ქაშვეთის წმინდა გიორგის სახელობის ტაძარი
voyage.content: A copy of 11th-century Samtavisi church. The Kashveti church was constructed between 1904 and 1910 by the architect L. Bilfeldt, who based his design on the medieval Samtavisi Cathedral. The construction was sponsored by the Georgian nobility and bourgeoisie. Kashveti was built on the site of a damaged church built of brick at the request of the Amilakhvari family in 1753. Significant contributions to the current chu

voyage.name: Synagogue
voyage.address: K. Leselidze street, 4? or Abkhazians Street.(კ. აფხაზის ქ.) #41
voyage.content: Functioning synagogue constructed in 1910. Women and men are seated separately.

voyage.name: Jumah Mosque
voyage.content: Turkish Sunni mosque, along the road from the Botanical Gardens to the Sulphur Baths. The usual dress code and entry restrictions for non-Muslims apply.

voyage.name: Holy Trinity Church
voyage.alt: Old Trinity Church, ძველი სამების ეკლესია
voyage.address: Erosi Manjgaladze Turn, Abashidze Street (აბაშიძის ქ.) # 4

voyage.name: Armenian Cathedral of S. Gevorg
voyage.content: Built in 1251 AD, and seat of the Armenian Archbishop of Georgia. Tomb of the famous Caucasian bard Sayat-Nova is in front of the church.

voyage.name: Norashen Armenian Church
voyage.content: Boarded up Armenian Church, used as a library in Soviet times. It was built in 1487, with a lot of new work in the mid-1600s.

voyage.name: Upper and Lower Bethlehem churches
voyage.alt: ზემო და ქვემო ბეთლემის ეკლესიები კლდისუბანი

voyage.name: Echmiadzin Armenian Church
voyage.content: Built in 1805, and later renovated.

voyage.name: Vank Armenian Monastery Belltower
voyage.content: This beautiful, tall belltower, hidden behind modern buildings near Carrefour is all that remains of the 14th century Vank Armenian Monastery, which had the largest church in Tbilisi until 1938 when it was torn down by the government. Somehow the belltower survived and pops up above the residential buildings at 3 Atoneli Street.

voyage.name: Chronicle of Georgia
voyage.content: An impressive memorial with a great view across Tbilisi and its lake. Also, a mesmerising walk through some past architecture. It consists of several giant statues and 16 30- to 35-m-tall columns at the top and a portrait of the life of Christ at the bottom part. There is also a chapel and a St. Nino cross. It was designed by Zurab Tsereteli in 1985 but was never fully finished. A hidden gem that many who have been h

voyage.name: Mother Georgia Monument
voyage.content: A 20-metre aluminium figure of a woman in Georgian national dress, ready to meet enemies or friends, she has a knife in one hand and a bowl of wine in the other. Erected on the Sololaki hill in 1958, Tbilisi's 1,500th birthday and designed by Elguja Amashukeli.

voyage.name: Mtatsminda Pantheon of Writers and Public Figures
voyage.content: Many famous writers, and the mother of Joseph Stalin, are buried here.

voyage.name: Old Tbilisi
voyage.content: Perhaps one of the most distinctive pleasures of walking through the Old City, with its old-style balconies, ancient churches, winding streets, and charming shops. Be prepared to see a number of eclectic sights, from the abandoned streetcar near Erekle Street to the art galleries of Chardini Street to the stunning modern art lining Sioni Street. Sub-neighborhoods include Sololaki, with its elegant restaurants and art

voyage.name: Vake Park Area
voyage.content: This is one of Tbilisi's posher districts, home to many immigrants and nouveaux riches. While not quite as atmospheric as Old Tbilisi, Vake is home to some lovely parks, pleasant nineteenth-century architecture, and some of the city's most high-end shopping, including luxury furniture store Missioni. There are also plenty of elegant, if understated, bars and restaurants in this area. In Vake there are two buildings o

voyage.name: Georgian National Academy of Sciences
voyage.address: Shota Rustaveli Ave. (შოთა რუსთაველის გამზ), #48 / Rustaveli Square

voyage.name: City Hall
voyage.content: Before City Hall stay the Monument of St. George

voyage.name: Presidential Palace
voyage.content: Inaugurated in summer 2009, an architectural monstrosity above the river, designed by Italian architect Michele De Luki. Guided tours may be booked seven work days in advance.

voyage.name: Theatre and Film University
voyage.alt: Shota Rustaveli Theatre and Film University / თეატრისა და კინოს სახელმწიფო უნივერსიტეტი

voyage.name: Library of the Parliament
voyage.alt: National Parliamentary Library of Georgia / საქართველოს პარლამენტის ბიბლიოთეკა

voyage.name: Caucasian House
voyage.content: Also an accommodation.

voyage.name: House of Writers
voyage.address: I l According Street (ი. მაჩაბლის ქ.) #11

voyage.name: Sulphur Baths
voyage.content: The main bath district is easy to spot with its small domes on ground level. There are several small baths offering different levels of comfort. The baths are relatively small, and you may have to wait for a pool to become available. English service is not guaranteed. Massages are available; however, they are more like a washing, but well worth it for the experience. You should bring your own towel and beach sandals

voyage.name: Bath No. 5
voyage.content: This is the only public bath in this area right at the beginning, follow the neon light. It is definitely worth the experience, so do not miss it. The men's section has a central shower area, a hot pool and a sauna. The women's public section only provides showers and massage, and are probably not worth it. Massage is 10 lari extra. Bring slippers and towel or rent them there for extra cost.

voyage.name: Turtle Lake (Kus T'ba)
voyage.content: This lake is in the hilly outskirts of Tbilisi. A popular weekend getaway for families, the lake offers pedal-boat rentals as well as swimming (deckchairs optional) for reasonable prices (swimming entry, without deckchair, is about 3 lari). Alright for a hot summer day, and offering views of the mountains and of the city below. Snackbars, restaurants and fruit cocktail shakers are available overlooking the lake. It's

voyage.name: Lake Lisi (Lisis T'ba)
voyage.content: Much further out than Turtle Lake (a cab will set you back about 10–15 lari each way), Lake Lisi is much larger and more remote, with long, winding mountain walks surrounding the lake. Unlike Turtle Lake, the entire Lake Lisi is opened up for swimmers. Be warned — there aren't always taxis waiting to take you back.

voyage.name: Climb up to the Narikala Fortress
voyage.content: The crumbling ruins of this once-great fortress, standing alongside the Upper Betelmi Churches and the stunning Botanical gardens, offer panoramic views of the city below. It's quite a steep climb, though you could take the cable car instead. Also while the lack of bureaucracy and guard-rails can be liberating for some, you may want to watch your step. Temporarily closed as of May 2024.

voyage.name: Botanical garden
voyage.content: National botanic garden of Georgia, founded in 1845. Lying in the Tsavkisis-Tskali Gorge near Narikala Fortress. The garden is big and inconsistently maintained. Some nice parts are the Waterfall and the path along the creek upstream in the Mediterranean collection. Also the Parterre in a Central Park is a hidden gem. A fun zipline for over 150 cm tall and under 110 kg sliders is available for 40 lari.

voyage.name: Mtatsminda park
voyage.content: to have fun with your kids, see the views of Tbilisi or to take a ride on the Ferris wheel. You need to buy an access card at a cashiers desk for 2 lari. Funicular ride is also 10 lari one way and you use the access card for that.

voyage.name: Alexander's Garden
voyage.content: A part of Park April.

voyage.name: Paragliding around Tbilisi
voyage.content: Find yourself (and your pilot) hanging in the sky with the clouds staring at the gorgeous sprawling Georgian Caucasus mountains below you.

voyage.name: Alexander Griboedov Russian State Drama Theatre
Tbilisi Opera and Ballet State Theatre
voyage.content: Beautiful opera house in neo-moorish building. Opera founded in 1851. Tickets (for some shows?) can be bought online at .

voyage.name: Rustaveli National Theater
voyage.alt: Shota Rustaveli Theater, შოთა რუსთაველის თეატრი

voyage.name: Tbilisi Marathon
voyage.price: Participation fee 10 lari/10 km and 15 lari/Half marathon
voyage.content: Held annually in October, with full & half-marathon, 10 km race and kids' runs. The start and finish is at Rustaveli Avenue. The last event was 27 September 2020 as a virtual marathon, the last traditional event was 29 September 2019. In 2022, it will be held on 25 September.

voyage.name: The flea market
voyage.hours: Every Sat, but seems to be every day nowadays until sunset
voyage.address: Dzveli Tbilisi, ~3 Zviad Gamsakhurdia Named Right Bank
voyage.content: This is one of the best places to get jewellery, antiques, antique swords, musical instruments, and electronics. Haggling is encouraged, although if you speak little Georgian or Russian you may experience the odd juxtaposition of bargaining for antiques using the type-pad of your vendor's mobile phone. Very popular with tourists, so prices are inflated.

voyage.name: Dezerter Bazaar
voyage.content: Sells everything, especially fruit, vegetable, cheese and churchkhela. Famous with tourists and locals likewise.

voyage.name: Station Square Underground Market
voyage.content: Sells mainly clothes, and has a lot of repair shops.

voyage.name: Didube Market
voyage.content: Has a large selection of cheap second hand clothes and shoes.

voyage.name: Station Square Bridge
voyage.content: Cloths and shoes can be found here. A pair of leather boots start at 40-50 lari.

voyage.name: Samgori Metro Underpass
voyage.content: The shops here specialise on used shoes.

voyage.name: 2nd hand outlet
voyage.content: A huge store of about 200 m² with all sorts of used good, mostly shoes and cloths, but also sports and camping equipment, and even a scooter.

voyage.name: Day Off! - Re-Use Store
voyage.content: Probably more posh than actual used, for the according extra lari.

voyage.name: Caucasian Carpets Gallery
voyage.content: A marvel of assorted carpets.

voyage.name: Pixel 34
voyage.content: Shopping Centre

voyage.name: Kolkhoz Square Underground Market
voyage.content: They sell home-made chacha and inexpensive churchkhela. Conveniently located near Liberty Square if you go back home from there (airport bus).

voyage.name: Kiwi Vegan Cafe
voyage.content: Vegan cafe. Low prices, delicious, has tofu.

voyage.name: Racha
voyage.content: Great and authentic Georgian restaurant. It is not fancy, but it is real and the food is tasty. An interesting place in the basement for unpretentious tourists who want to eat inexpensively. The menu offers a selection of national dishes. You can feel the atmosphere of Georgia here.

voyage.name: Veliaminov
voyage.content: Restaurant with Georgian cuisine. It has the most delicious khinkali.

voyage.name: Family kitchen
voyage.content: Delicious dishes and comfortable atmosphere. There are options for those who don't eat meat. It works like in a canteen.

voyage.name: Good Mood Food
voyage.content: Small eatery serving different kinds of Khachapuri.

voyage.name: Tom Yum Thai Food
voyage.content: Excellent authentic Thai dishes, everything very tasty. The interior is rather simple.

voyage.name: Shawarma
voyage.content: A delicious no-name shawarma joint nestled amongst the pricier tourist-oriented restaurants.

voyage.name: Fire Wok Dadiani
voyage.content: Nurse that hangover with some greasy Asian noodles. No seating.

voyage.name: Klike's Khinkali
voyage.content: An excellent underground khinkali spot, popular among locals.

voyage.name: Joker Shaurma
voyage.content: delicious shawarma and tasty kebab.

voyage.name: Dzveli Sakhli Restaurant (Old House)
voyage.content: Live traditional Georgian music and singing starts at around 18:00 every day, although it's also the perfect place for a quiet post-flea market weekend lunch. Stunning river-views and faux-rural atmosphere — enormous portions at relatively reasonable prices. Credit cards accepted.

voyage.name: Cafe Gabriadze
voyage.content: Formerly the trendy "Sans Souci," this artsy eatery (owned by master puppeteer Gabriadze) has reopened after a lengthy renovation period. With a quirkily bohemian decor and inventive takeoffs of classic Georgian dishes (just try their lobio!), the fare here is a cut above the standard khachapuri-and-khinkhali dinner options.

voyage.name: Kala
voyage.content: Hip cafe/restaurant with live Jazz most evenings. Wi–Fi; credit card payment accepted. Check the ratings.

voyage.name: Khinkali House
voyage.content: All Khinkali, all the time. Does a wide range of other Georgian food too. The entrance isn't obvious, you have to enter an alleyway at No. 37 and then go down some steps into a courtyard.

voyage.name: Cafe Flowers
voyage.content: Sporting stunning views, the terrace at Cafe Flowers (so named for the flora that adorn the terrace and adjacent garden) overlooks the Old Town from across the river. Food is generally good, although be wary of dairy-based dishes lest you come down with an upset stomach.

voyage.name: Cafe Leila
voyage.content: Charming pescatarian cafe with vegan options. Serves vegan wine. Tables outside and good decor inside.

voyage.name: Multifunctional Space - Theatre
voyage.content: The “Theatre” is a multifunctional space with a completely new concept, where you can simultaneously experience a classic cabaret, see an American musical, enjoy opera and ballet performances, attend a concert and listen to the works of modern artists. Tourists can also discover Georgian cultural attractions accompanied by gastronomy.

voyage.name: Tsiskvili
voyage.content: "Ethno Tsiskvili" is not just a restaurant; it is a unique place with an extraordinary exterior and interior. It can be likened to a museum, with each aspect reflecting Georgian culture and history. What sets Ethno Tsiskvili apart is its natural waterfall on the premises, adding to the overall ambiance. Additionally, the restaurant offers a daily program that combines unique Georgian dance and folklore, further enhan

voyage.name: Picasso Restaurant
voyage.content: Chinese cuisine

voyage.name: Shandiz Restaurant
voyage.hours: Club Thu-Sun from 20:00; karaoke bar daily from 19:00; restaurant daily from 11:00
voyage.content: Sushi + night club + Middle Eastern atmosphere, 4 floors. Cocktail Bar, and BBQ.

voyage.name: Baan Thai
voyage.content: This is the most authentic Thai restaurant in the city, and a favorite of local immigrants. Operated by a friendly Thai woman, it has good food and quick service, but it's easy to miss because it's on an unremarkable street between the Opera house and Radisson hotel.

voyage.name: Cafe Canape
voyage.content: Reasonably priced, charming bistro with fusion French-Georgian cuisine and a neighborhood-y atmosphere. Definitely a brunch place for Vake's "smart set". The khachapuri is out-of-this-world.

voyage.name: Obrigado Tasco
voyage.content: Cozy and authentic Portuguese restaurant focused on traditional petiscos, francesinha, bifana, and Portuguese wines, hosted by a welcoming Portuguese owner.

voyage.name: Ronny's Pizza
voyage.content: Lunch, dinner, delivery, take out and catering. Ronny's pizza comes in personal size, regular (12 inch) or extra large (18inch) Delivery charge based on kilometers all over Tbilisi. Classic American style pizza with mozzarella.

voyage.name: Fiorino
voyage.content: Fiorino offers best pizzas in Tbilisi, one of the best carpaccios and veal. Relaxing environment and outdoor seating.

voyage.name: Prego
voyage.address: Three locations (Saburtalo, intersection of Vazha-Pshavela and Pekini St.; Vake, on Paliashvili, just below the round (UN) garden and the third in the old town, Erekle II st.)
voyage.content: Prices are said to be reasonable and service is usually good. Look out for the daily specials - usually a bit pricier, but worth it.

voyage.name: Piano
voyage.content: This new Italian eatery feels more like a swank New York restaurant than a Georgian-style trattoria, with black-and-white Botticelli-inspired wallpaper and uber-trendy minimalist light fixtures. The food is reasonably priced for the — admittedly expensive — area, but it's good (especially the super-fresh tomato-based sauces) and air-conditioned to boot. Beware of the bread; it's so delicious, you'll be full before yo

voyage.name: Prospero's Bookstore and Caliban's Coffehouse
voyage.content: With wireless internet, a bucolic courtyard, and spotless furnishings, this expat bookstore-cum-coffeehouse could be in London's Notting Hill. Good selection of English books, but the real gem is the atmosphere - a perfect escape for when Tbilisi's more chaotic pleasures start to become overwhelming. Effectively bilingual waitstaff, try to strike up conversations with other foreigners.

voyage.name: Strada
voyage.content: A mix of contemporary Asian and American cuisine.

voyage.name: Rigi Gastrodouqan
voyage.content: Georgian cuisine with a modern twist.

voyage.name: Ninia's Garden
voyage.content: Excellent Georgian cuisine nestled in a cozy garden.

voyage.name: Fabrika courtyard
voyage.content: A large courtyard filled with bars and cafes. Packed at night with locals and tourists alike.

voyage.name: Wine Factory N1
voyage.content: Another courtyard with numerous bars and restaurants, a bit lower key than Fabrika

voyage.name: Meoba Bar
voyage.content: A hip cocktail joint, popular with locals and not bad on the prices.

voyage.name: Lolita
voyage.content: Popular restaurant by day, cracking bar by night.

voyage.name: 41 Gradus
voyage.content: Small stylish cocktail bar serving their own creations. Slide the metal door to get downstairs.

voyage.name: Alibi Room
voyage.content: Cheap bar well known (or infamous) among locals, attracts a young crowd and gets packed on Fridays, when things can get a bit rough; so it's not for the faint hearted. '

voyage.name: Dublin
voyage.content: Irish pub with live music from 20:00-00:00. Try the meat wrapped in bacon.

voyage.name: Over Bar
voyage.content: Cozy with lots of diverse drinks and bar snacks.

voyage.name: Gallery Café
voyage.content: A bar with DJs and live music for students and hip people. Retro and used look interior. Also cool to hang out during the day.

voyage.name: Hangar Bar
voyage.content: Irish pub run by an American couple. Very popular among immigrants.

voyage.name: Kazbegi Beer
voyage.hours: Ostensibly 10:00-23:00 daily, but has been known to close early
voyage.content: Legendary. Large beer cafe frequented mostly by locals but also the famous "beer wall" where bottles will be filled with beer of your choosing from a hose.

voyage.name: Mozaika
voyage.content: Very nice bar with nice and hip people, and some vegetarian food. Pretty easy to get into conversation with locals here. The bar has two floors and a balcony for smokers, but it is often very packed. The beer prices are low to reasonable.

voyage.name: Old London
voyage.content: Live music every evening.

voyage.name: Sakhelosno
voyage.content: Crowded underground dive, alternative/student vibe, with cheap and tasty peach chacha, and (at least on weekends) excellent karaoke singing.

voyage.name: Singer
voyage.content: Jazz bar and restaurant with great live music, mostly for elder and settled people. In summer you might just hang around on the square in front and enjoy the music with a beer from the local shop.

voyage.name: Success bar
voyage.content: Mostly a gay bar with affordable cocktails and club for diverse crowd with drag shows, karaoke and alike. Well worth a visit if you are bored with packed Mozaika. Nice latex sofas.

voyage.name: Warszawa bar
voyage.content: Polish bar with a nice atmosphere, popular with young people. 2 lari beer, decent selection of other drinks.

voyage.name: Althaus Tea
voyage.content: Nice and cosy café with interesting sublevel. Good during colder times.

voyage.name: Laghidze Waters
voyage.content: Small cafe selling the (reasonably) famous Laghidze Waters and a range of Georgian pastry snacks quite cheap (3–7 lari for a pastry). The other Laghidze Waters cafe near Sameba Cathedral seems to be closed as of 3/19 so this is the only one in Tbilisi.

voyage.name: Minimalist
voyage.content: Interesting tiny café with attached gallery that serves coffee in various different ways (cold brew, French press, filter, ePebo, Moccha, etc.). Though, the type of coffee they have is quite sour ... not an expert though.

voyage.name: Unity Kava
voyage.content: Great coffee with minimal seating.

voyage.name: Plant Lovers Tbilisi
voyage.content: A gardening shop that also has incredible coffee and delicious homemade baked goods, for some reason.

voyage.name: Museum Cafe
voyage.content: Good coffee and good food in a comfortable seating environment. A nice place to open the laptop and knock out some work. Hours are a bit unpredictable.

voyage.name: Bassiani
voyage.price: 30 lari entry (if the bouncer lets you in)
voyage.content: A famous underground techno club, possibly one of the best in the whole region—think Berghain. It also has an LGBT night, clearly stating its modernness and openness. Don't go if the latter does upset you in any way! FB.

voyage.name: Buddha Bar
voyage.content: Opened in March 2012. Latest arm of Buddha Bar Asian-inspired restaurant/lounge chain. Reservations are highly encouraged and sometimes a must. Reservations can be called in after 12:00 daily. An excellent place for sushi and good lounge and electronic music.

voyage.name: Cubic
voyage.content: One of the best places for good house music, real minimal techno and sometimes some breakbeats and dnb.

voyage.name: Drama Bar
voyage.content: Another interesting club with DnB sometimes. A good option if the do not close soon and you don't want to head out to Bassiani or Khidi.

voyage.name: Guru Club
voyage.content: Foreign DJs and singers & G.U.R.U. show girls

voyage.name: KalaKuri Restaurant/Club
voyage.hours: Club: Fri and Sat from 23:00; Restaurant: 12:00–13:00; Lounge Bar: 17:00–03:00
voyage.content: Good night club, pop, 90s and modern music.

voyage.name: KHIDI
voyage.content: If you do not get into Bassiani, head here. However, reviews are complaining about an excess of guys. So, better to be female or to bring your "own" if you are into meeting straight people.

voyage.name: Night Flight
voyage.content: Supposedly has the best house, trance, dance, club music, Georgian and foreign DJs in Tbilisi. Drinks are a bit expensive, but worth it.

voyage.name: George Apartment
voyage.address: Intersection Tsinamdzgvrishvili Street ~53 and Giorgi Mazniashvili St
voyage.content: Warm reception. Wifi.

voyage.name: Backpackers Hostel
voyage.address: no.11, Machabeli St. Old Tbilisi district
voyage.content: Hostel in the old city, Kitchen, laundry services, common room. It is one of the cheapest places in town but has trouble with drifters.

voyage.name: Boombully Rooms & Hostel
voyage.content: It's in historical downtown, near many city attractions and the Old town District, a block away from Prospero’s Books. The property is in a historical building with many green, eco-friendly and sustainable elements, like vintage and re-purposed furniture. The sign on the front of building for Boombully isn't the most noticeable, so watch the building addresses as you pass them.

voyage.name: Terrace Hostel Tbilisi
voyage.content: Friendly people, amazing view of the city, free wi-fi, possible airport transport for $20.

voyage.name: Envoy Hostel
voyage.content: Boasting a large terrace with a view of the city. Their staff speak excellent English and are very knowledgeable and helpful. Newly renovated and clean, it has a high ratio of bathrooms per beds. Breakfast is offered daily, although it will cost you 10 or so lari. Wi-fi, laundry service, tours, airport pick up and air conditioning, and central heating.

voyage.name: Fox Hostel
voyage.content: Hostel with kitchen access, pets, fox motifs on the walls.

voyage.name: Hostel FreeStyle
voyage.content: Small, friendly hostel in one of the nicest neighbourhoods of Tbilisi, Chugureti. Close to Marjanishvili metro, family atmosphere and nice social area. Beds perhaps aren't the most comfortable but a thick blanket over the mattress helps a good bit. Has a very cute cat.

voyage.name: Friends Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm from 7 lari, privates from 30 lari
voyage.address: Betlemi Str. #28-30, entrance up from ascent Tumaniani street 9
voyage.content: Near the Narikhala Fortress, surrounded by the traditional balconied Georgian houses and architecture. The building itself is a historic one, with old-styled interior. 10 beds in dorm and 2 privates. Nice balcony and common area (though a little dark), Old Town view, bar, BBQ area, guest kitchen. Two showers. Worth while if you get a bargain deal.

voyage.name: Green Stairs Hostel
voyage.content: Free Wi-Fi and a communal fridge. The hostel is very simple, but run by a nice couple who speak English. It's a little cold in the winter, but each room does have a space heater. The owner will drive you to the airport for 25 lari.

voyage.name: Old Town Hostel
voyage.content: Comfortable beds, clean, cozy, and friendly hostel. Airport transfer is possible.

voyage.name: Rest Hostel Tbilisi
voyage.content: Has 3 private rooms with shared bathroom, a total of 7 beds and one extra bed. Luggage storage, 24-hour reception (you may need to call, though), Internet, computers, free Wi-Fi in room, cable TV/DVD, free towels, linen included, air conditioning, guest kitchen, shared bathroom/shower, laundry. Car service 4WD, and can organize tours to the North-West.

voyage.name: "New Tbilisi" Hostel
voyage.content: Run by ex-backpackers. Popular among young backpackers, particularly those who are very price-conscious. Can be crowded and noisy. Free Internet & Wi-Fi; guest kitchen; cheap laundry service. Advertises itself as a 'party hotel'.

voyage.name: Tbilisi Rooms Hostel & Tours
voyage.content: Hostel is clean and has both private rooms and dormitories, equipped kitchen for self catering, free tea and coffee, free Wi-fi, laundry (3 lari), and two shared bathrooms. The friendly staff speak English, Georgian, and Russian.

voyage.name: Hotel at Gomi 19
voyage.content: Cozy rooms, big living room, kitchen and balcony with incredible view. 24h reception, fan, airport transfers (11 EUR), BBQ area, bicycle parking, cable TV, free parking, free Wi-Fi, laundry, linen and towels included, lockers, luggage storage, tours/travel desk.

voyage.name: Beaumonde
voyage.content: Nice B&B with balconies and a roof deck. The breakfast and dinner are very filling. There is free internet. The family that runs the hotel is very warm and welcoming. Staff speaks Georgian, Russian, and some English.

voyage.name: Betsy's Hotel
voyage.content: Hotel with 57 rooms, 4 star going on 3, often booked out for conferences.

voyage.name: British House
